test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Plaster of Paris is prepared when:

options.text: brine is heated at 373 K and it loses water molecules
ammonia is heated at 373 K and it loses water molecules
soda lime is heated at 373 K and it loses water molecules
gypsum is heated at 373 K and it loses water molecules

solution:
The correct answer is __**gypsum is heated at 373 K and it loses water molecules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plaster of Paris is chemically known as calcium sulfate hemihydrate.
 
• It is prepared by heating gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) at about 373 K (100°C).
 
• During this process, gypsum loses water molecules to form Plaster of Paris.
 
• The chemical equation for this process is:

 CaSO₄·2H₂O (gypsum) → CaSO₄·0.5H₂O (Plaster of Paris) + 1.5H₂O

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum**: A mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate, with the chemical formula CaSO₄·2H₂O.
 
• **Calcium sulfate hemihydrate**: The chemical name for Plaster of Paris, with the formula CaSO₄·0.5H₂O.
 
• **Uses of Plaster of Paris**: Commonly used for making sculptures, molds, and casts; also in construction for finishing walls and ceilings.
 
• **Setting reaction**: When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris rehydrates and sets into a hard solid, reforming into gypsum.
 
• **Temperature control**: The heating temperature must be controlled carefully to ensure proper formation of Plaster of Paris without decomposing it to anhydrous calcium sulfate.
